Pump Controller Operation Manual
================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
----------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout before servicing the pump motor.
- Verify zero electrical potential at the disconnect before removing panels.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working with pressurized systems.
- Never bypass safety interlocks or emergency stop controls.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
-------------------
- The pump motor starts when the green START button is pressed.
- Motor runs until the red STOP button is pressed or an fault is detected.
- Normal operating pressure range: 20-50 PSI.
- Flow rate: 0-100 GPM depending on impeller size.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
-------------------
a. Confirm all safety guards are in place.
b. Verify lubrication oil level is between MIN and MAX marks on sight glass.
c. Confirm discharge valve is open before motor start.
d. Press GREEN START button to begin pump operation.
e. Monitor pressure gauge to confirm pressure builds within normal range.
f. Listen for unusual noises indicating cavitation or misalignment.

4. INSPECTION PHASE
-------------------
- Check pump housing for leaks, cracks, or damage.
- Inspect mechanical seals for wear or fluid seepage.
- Verify bearing temperature is within normal range (below 80°C).
- Inspect coupling alignment between motor and pump shaft.
- Check foundation bolts for tightness.
- Verify alignment laser reading is within tolerance.

5. LUBRICATION
--------------
- Oil type: ISO VG 32 synthetic compressor oil.
- Oil level: Must be between MIN and MAX marks on sight glass.
- Lubrication interval: Every 500 operating hours.
- Oil change interval: Every 2000 operating hours or annually.
- Before adding oil, clean the fill port and surrounding area.
- After oil change, prime the lubrication system and check for leaks.

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------
PROBLEM: Pump will not start
- Cause: Power not supplied - check voltage at disconnect, verify fuses.
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop station.
- Cause: Motor protection trip - reset thermal overload relay.
- Cause: Control circuit fault - inspect wiring and control relays.

PROBLEM: Low pressure output
- Cause: Discharge valve partially closed - open valve fully.
- Cause: Worn impeller - inspect and replace if necessary.
- Cause: Air leak in suction line - tighten fittings, check seals.
- Cause: Clogged filter - clean or replace filter element.

PROBLEM: Excessive vibration
- Cause: Misalignment between motor and pump - realign using laser tool.
- Cause: Unbalanced impeller - inspect and rebalance or replace.
- Cause: Worn bearings - replace bearings.
- Cause: Loose foundation bolts - tighten and re-level unit.

PROBLEM: Oil discoloration or contamination
- Cause: Oil decomposition from overheating - replace oil.
- Cause: Water ingress - inspect seals, fix leaks, replace oil.
- Cause: Foreign particles in oil - clean sumple, replace filter, flush system.

7. SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE
---------------------
a. Gradually reduce load if pump is under load.
b. Press RED STOP button to stop motor.
c. Close discharge valve after motor stops.
d. Allow pump to cool if recently under load.
e. Lockout-tagout for any subsequent maintenance.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Visual inspection for leaks, unusual noises, vibration.
- Every 500 hours: Check oil level, inspect filters, check bearing temperature.
- Every 2000 hours: Oil change, detailed inspection of seals and bearings.
- Every 5000 hours: Comprehensive overhaul, replace wear parts as needed.
- Annual: Full safety inspection, certification of interlocks and E-stops.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Pump overpressure: Immediately press E-stop, isolate power.
- Fire near pump: Evacuate area, call fire department, do not attempt extinguishment without qualified personnel.
- Chemical spill: Contain spill, notify environmental safety, follow MSDS procedures.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: PC-350 Industrial Pump Controller
- Motor power: 15 HP, 3-phase, 230/460V
- Operating temperature: -20°C to 40°C
- Protection class: IP55
- Connection: NEMA 4X enclosure
- Flow range: 5-100 GPM
- Pressure range: 20-50 PSI
- Material: Cast iron housing, stainless steel shaft

HVAC Maintenance Controller Operation Manual
============================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
---------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout on electrical power before servicing HVAC units.
- Verify zero electrical potential at disconnect before removing panels.
- Recover refrigerant per EPA regulations before opening refrigerant circuit.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working with refrigerants, electrical components, and moving parts.
- Never bypass safety controls or temperature limiters.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
--------------------
- System provides heating when heating mode is selected and thermostat calls for heat.
- System provides cooling when cooling mode is selected and thermostat calls for cool.
- Normal supply air temperature range: 55-75°F cooling, 90-120°F heating.
- Fan operates at variable speed: 0-100% depending on demand.
- Air filter should be checked monthly and replaced when dirty.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE (HEATING)
------------------------------
a. Confirm thermostat is set to HEAT mode and temperature is above current room temperature.
b. Verify gas supply is on (for gas-fired units) or electrical connections are secure (for electric units).
c. Inspect air filter - replace if dirty or restricted.
d. Check that all access panels are secure and guards are in place.
e. Set thermostat to desired temperature.
f. System should initiate ignition sequence after 30-second pre-purge.
g. Verify flame is established and burners are operating normally.
h. Monitor supply air temperature rises to normal range within 5 minutes.
i. Fan will begin blowing heated air once heat exchanger reaches safe temperature.

4. STARTUP SEQUENCE (COOLING)
-------------------------------
a. Confirm thermostat is set to COOL mode and temperature is below current room temperature.
b. Verify electrical connections are secure and power is supplied to compressor.
c. Inspect air filter - replace if dirty or restricted.
d. Check that all access panels are secure and guards are in place.
e. Set thermostat to desired temperature.
f. Compressor should start after thermostat call for cool.
g. Verify condenser fan is operating.
h. Check that supply air temperature drops to normal range within 5 minutes.
i. System will cycle on and off to maintain setpoint.

5. INSPECTION PHASE
--------------------
- Check air filter condition and airflow - replace if dirty.
- Inspect supply and return registers for obstructions.
- Check thermostat calibration and operation.
- Inspect evaporator coil for frost or ice formation (cooling mode).
- Inspect heat exchanger for cracks or damage (heating mode).
- Verify refrigerant lines for leaks (trace with detector solution).
- Check blower motor and fan for unusual noise or vibration.
- Inspect ductwork for leaks, loose connections, or damage.
- Verify safety controls are functional (limit switches, pressure controls).

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

PROBLEM: System will not start (heating)
- Cause: Thermostat not calling for heat - check settings.
- Cause: No gas supply (gas units) - verify gas valve is open.
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage at disconnect, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: Flame failure - reset after safety lockout, inspect burner.
- Cause: Limit switch tripped - reset after addressing root cause.

PROBLEM: System will not start (cooling)
- Cause: Thermostat not calling for cool - check settings.
- Cause: Compressor protection trip - reset thermal overload.
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: Refrigerant low - system may have leak, require recharge.
- Cause: High-pressure switch tripped - reset after addressing cause.

PROBLEM: Insufficient heating
- Cause: Dirty air filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Thermostat not calibrated - recalibrate or replace.
- Cause: Gas pressure too low - adjust gas valve, check supply.
- Cause: Heat exchanger restricted - clean or replace.
- Cause: Duct leaks - seal ductwork, insulate as needed.

PROBLEM: Insufficient cooling
- Cause: Dirty air filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Dirty evaporator coil - clean coil.
- Cause: Dirty condenser coil - clean outdoor unit coil.
- Cause: Refrigerant low - system has leak, locate and repair, recharge.
- Cause: High outdoor temperature - system may not meet load demand.
- Cause: Thermostat not calibrated - recalibrate or replace.

PROBLEM: Short cycling (frequent on/off)
- Cause: Oversized system for space - may require load calculation.
- Cause: Dirty filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Thermostat located near heat source - relocate thermostat.
- Cause: Low refrigerant - system has leak, locate and repair, recharge.
- Cause: High static pressure in ductwork - redesign duct system.

PROBLEM: compressor will not start
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: compressor protection trip - reset thermal overload after cooling.
- Cause: capacitor failure - replace capacitor.
- Cause: contactor failure - replace contactor.
- Cause: thermostat not calling - check settings and wiring.

7. REFRIGERANT SERVICE
------------------------
- Recover refrigerant: Use certified recovery machine per EPA Section 608.
- Leak detection: Electronic leak detector or trace with Nitrogen soap solution.
- Recharge: Add only specified refrigerant type and amount per nameplate.
- Never mix refrigerant types.
- Document all refrigerant additions and removals per regulatory requirements.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Check thermostat operation, listen for unusual noises, verify airflow.
- Every 250 hours: Check air filter, inspect visual condition of unit.
- Every 500 hours: Clean or replace air filter, inspect evaporator/condenser coils.
- Every 1000 hours: Check refrigerant pressure, test safety controls, lubricate motors.
- Every 2000 hours: Clean burners (gas units), inspect heat exchanger, check belt tension.
- Annual: Full combustion analysis (gas units), refrigerant charge verification, complete safety inspection.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Refrigerant leak: Evacuate area, ventilate, call qualified HVAC technician.
- Electrical fire: Cut power at disconnect, call fire department, do not use water on electrical.
- Gas leak (gas units): Evacuate area, ventilate, do not operate electrical switches, call gas company.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: HVAC-400 Maintenance Controller
- Capacity: 2-ton to 20-ton variable capacity
- Voltage: 208/240V single-phase or 208/3-phase
- Refrigerant: R-410A (or approved alternate)
- Airflow range: 400-2000 CFM
- Temperature range: -10°F to 120°F ambient
- Protection class: NEMA 1 (indoor), NEMA 3R (outdoor units)
- Connection: Standard HVAC plug-in connections
- Motor: ECM variable-speed blower motor
- Compressor: Scroll type, 2-20 HP

Warehouse Conveyor Controller Operation Manual
==============================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
---------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout before servicing conveyor drive system.
- Verify zero mechanical energy stored in springs or counterweights before removing guards.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working around moving conveyors.
- Never bypass safety interlocks or emergency stop controls.
- Ensure no personnel are on or near the conveyor before startup.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
--------------------
- Conveyor starts when the green START button is pressed.
- Stops when the red STOP button is pressed or an fault is detected.
- Normal operating speed: 0-150 FPM (feet per minute).
- Load capacity: 0-5000 lbs depending on belt type.
- Belt tracking should be checked at startup and weekly.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
-------------------
a. Confirm all safety guards are in place and secured.
b. Verify no personnel are on the conveyor belt.
c. Confirm drive is not in manual emergency stop mode.
d. Press GREEN START button to begin conveyor operation.
e. Monitor belt tracking - adjust tracking rollers if belt centers.
f. Listen for unusual noises indicating bearing or drive issues.
g. Verify belt moves smoothly without slippage.

4. INSPECTION PHASE
-------------------
- Check belt surface for cuts, tears, or excessive wear.
- Inspect belt tracking and centering - adjust idler rollers as needed.
- Check drive belt tension - should have 1/2" deflection under firm push.
- Inspect rollers and idlers for smooth rotation and no visible damage.
- Verify safety edge sensors are functional (press to test).
- Check motor housing for overheating signs.
- Inspect chain drives for proper tension and lubrication.
- Verify emergency stop buttons are functional at all control stations.

5. LUBRICATION
--------------
- bearing lubrication: Every 250 operating hours.
- Use: Lithium-based grease, NLGI Grade 2.
- Apply to roller bearings at each bearing location.
- Grease quantity: Until slightly excess appears at seal.
- Conveyor chain: Apply chain lubricant every 500 operating hours.
- Do not over-lubricate - excess attracts dust and debris.

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

PROBLEM: Conveyor will not start
- Cause: Power not supplied - check voltage at disconnect, verify fuses.
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop at nearest station.
- Cause: Motor protection trip - reset thermal overload relay.
- Cause: Control circuit fault - inspect wiring and control relays.
- Cause: Belt jam preventing motor start - clear obstruction.

PROBLEM: Belt slippage
- Cause: Drive belt too loose - tighten to 1/2" deflection.
- Cause: Worn drive belt - replace with new belt.
- Cause: Contaminated belt surface - clean with appropriate solvent.
- Cause: Overloaded system - reduce load, verify capacity limits.

PROBLEM: Belt tracking issues
- Cause: Misaligned tracking rollers - adjust left/right rollers.
- Cause: Uneven belt wear - rotate or replace belt.
- Cause: Material build-up on rollers - clean roller surfaces.
- Cause: Belt damaged or stretched - replace belt.

PROBLEM: Unexpected stoppage
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop.
- Cause: Thermal overload trip - reset after cooling.
- Cause: Power fluctuation - check supply voltage.
- Cause: Sensor fault - inspect safety edges and limit switches.

PROBLEM: Unusual noise
- Cause: Bearing failure - replace bearings.
- Cause: Loose chain or belt tension - adjust tension.
- Cause: Foreign object in conveyor path - remove obstruction.
- Cause: Motor mounting loose - tighten mounting bolts.

7. SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE
---------------------
a. Gradually reduce load if conveyor is under load.
b. Press RED STOP button to stop motor.
c. Allow belt to come to complete stop.
d. Lockout-tagout for any subsequent maintenance.
e. Remove any remaining material from belt.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Visual inspection for wear, tracking, unusual noises.
- Every 250 hours: Lubricate bearings, check belt tension.
- Every 500 hours: Inspect belt surface, clean rollers, test E-stops.
- Every 1000 hours: Replace drive belt, lubricate chain.
- Every 2000 hours: Comprehensive inspection of all rollers and idlers.
- Annual: Full safety certification of interlocks and E-stops.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Person on conveyor: Immediately press E-stop, do not attempt rescue until motion stops.
- Fire near conveyor: Evacuate area, call fire department.
- Material spill: Stop conveyor, contain spill, clean per warehouse protocols.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: WC-200 Warehouse Conveyor Controller
- Motor power: 5 HP, single-phase, 120/240V
- Belt speed: 0-150 FPM variable
- Load capacity: 5000 lbs maximum
- Belt width: 24 inches
- Power supply: 120V AC, 60 Hz
- Protection class: IP54
- Connection: NEMA 12 enclosure
- Roller spacing: 3 feet on center
- Emergency stop stations: At each end and mid-point

Fictional Machine Safety Procedures
=====================================

1. GENERAL SAFETY PRINCIPLES
-----------------------------
- Lockout-tagout (LOTO) must be performed before any maintenance activity.
- Never bypass or disable safety interlocks or emergency stop controls.
- All personnel must be trained on hazards before operating equipment.
- Safety procedures apply to all equipment types regardless of size or capacity.
- Emergency procedures must be posted at each workstation.

2. LOCKOUT-TAGOUT (LOTO) PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------
STEP 1: PREPARATION
- Identify all energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, mechanical, thermal).
- Verify the authorized personnel and required equipment for the LOTO.
- Review the equipment-specific LOTO procedure before beginning.

STEP 2: SHUTDOWN
- Stop the equipment using the normal shutdown procedure.
- Allow moving parts to come to complete stop.
- Disconnect process material from equipment.

STEP 3: ISOLATION
- Identify all energy isolation points (disconnect switches, valves, breakers).
- Operate all isolation devices to isolate equipment from energy sources.
- Verify isolation by attempting normal startup (equipment should not start).

STEP 4: APPLICATION OF LOCKOUT DEVICES
- Apply personal lockout device to each isolated energy point.
- Each technician applies their own lock with personal key/code.
- Verify each lock is properly seated and secured.

STEP 5: APPLICATION OF TAGS
- Apply personal tag with technician name, date, and reason.
- Tags must be visible and legible.
- Never remove another person's lock or tag without authorization.

STEP 6: RELEASE OF STORED ENERGY
- Release residual mechanical energy (springs, counterweights, gravity).
- Drain hydraulic/pneumatic systems to zero pressure.
- Allow capacitors to discharge (verify with meter).
- Open bleed valves to relieve pneumatic/hydraulic pressure.

STEP 7: VERIFICATION
- Attempt normal equipment startup to verify isolation.
- Verify all energy sources are zero or isolated.
- Confirm no one is near the equipment before proceeding.

3. EMERGENCY STOP (E-STOP) PROCEDURE
---------------------------------------
- Press E-STOP button immediately when hazard detected.
- E-STOP must cut power to all moving functions immediately.
- After E-STOP activation, confirm motion has ceased before approaching.
- E-STOP reset must only be performed after hazard is resolved.
- Only the person who activated E-STOP (or authorized rescue personnel) should reset.

4. MACHINE-SPECIFIC SAFETY PROCEDURES
---------------------------------------
PROCEDURE A: PUMP MAINTENANCE
- Perform LOTO on pump motor electrical supply.
- Verify zero voltage at disconnect before removing panels.
- Drain any fluid from pump housing before opening.
- Support any suspended components before removal.

PROCEDURE B: CONVEYOR MAINTENANCE
- Perform LOTO on conveyor drive electrical supply.
- Verify zero voltage at disconnect before entering conveyor zone.
- Secure conveyor belt to prevent accidental movement.
- Lock out all drive motors and associated control circuits.

PROCEDURE C: HVAC UNIT MAINTENANCE
- Perform LOTO on electrical supply and gas line (if gas-fired).
- Recover refrigerant per EPA regulations before opening circuit.
- Verify zero electrical potential and zero gas pressure.
- Support access panels before removal.

PROCEDURE D: BATTERY SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
- Perform LOTO on charger and load circuits.
- Verify zero voltage at battery terminals.
- Remove conductive jewelry, use insulated tools.
- Ensure adequate ventilation before beginning work.

5. CONFINED SPACE ENTRY
-------------------------
- Test atmosphere for oxygen deficiency and toxic gases.
- Verify forced ventilation is operating.
- Attend observer must be stationed outside confined space.
- Retrieval equipment must be available and functional.
- Permit system must be completed before entry.

6. HOT WORK PERMIT
--------------------
- Fire watch must be posted during and 30 minutes after hot work.
- Fire extinguishing equipment must be immediately available.
- Combustible materials must be removed from work area or protected.
- Hot work permit must be completed and authorized before beginning.

7. CHEMICAL HANDLING
--------------------
- Review Safety Data Sheet (SDS) before handling any chemical.
- Use appropriate PPE per SDS recommendations.
- Store chemicals in designated areas, properly labeled.
- In case of spill, follow spill containment procedure.
- Dispose of chemical waste per regulatory requirements.

8. PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
----------------------------------------
- Safety glasses with side shields must be worn at all times in work areas.
- Steel-toed boots required where heavy objects may fall.
- Hearing protection where noise levels exceed 85 dB(A).
- Gloves appropriate for hazard (chemical, thermal, electrical).
- Hard hats where overhead hazards exist.
- Respiratory protection where airborne contaminants exceed PEL.

9. INCIDENT REPORTING
----------------------
- All incidents, near-misses, and safety violations must be reported within 24 hours.
- Supervisor must investigate all incidents within 48 hours.
- Root cause analysis required for any recordable incident.
- Corrective actions must be implemented and verified.
- Incident reports must be retained for minimum 3 years.

10. SAFETY TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
----------------------------------
- Initial safety training before first assignment.
- Annual refresher training on all safety procedures.
- Task-specific training before performing new procedures.
- Emergency drill participation quarterly.
- LOTO certification renewed annually.
- Emergency response training semi-annually.

Battery Monitoring Unit Operation Manual
========================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
---------------------
- Always observe polarity when connecting or disconnecting battery terminals.
- Remove watches, rings, and metal jewelry before working on battery systems.
- Use insulated tools rated for electrical work.
- Work in well-ventilated areas - hydrogen gas may be present during charging.
- Never short battery terminals - can cause sparks, heat, or explosion.
- Wear acid-resistant gloves and eye protection when handling lead-acid batteries.
- Verify charging system is disconnected before performing maintenance.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
--------------------
- Battery voltage (fully charged): 12.6-12.8V (12V system) or 25.2-25.6V (24V system)
- Charge voltage: 14.4-14.8V (12V system) or 28.8-29.6V (24V system)
- Discharge cutoff: 10.5V (12V) or 21.0V (24V)
- Charge current: Limited by charger specification (typically 10-20% of Ah capacity)
- Operating temperature range: -20°C to 50°C (performance degrades above 30°C)
- State-of-health (SOH) threshold for replacement: <80% of rated capacity

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
--------------------
a. Visually inspect battery for damage, cracks, or leakage.
b. Verify battery is correctly polarized (positive/+ and negative/-).
c. Confirm terminal connections are tight and free of corrosion.
d. Check electrolyte levels (flooded types only) - add distilled water if low.
e. Connect charger or load as appropriate.
f. Monitor voltage and current during initial charge/discharge.
g. Verify all monitoring readings are within normal range.

4. INSPECTION PHASE
--------------------
- Check battery case for cracks, swelling, or distortion.
- Inspect terminal connections for corrosion, looseness, or heat damage.
- Clean terminals with baking soda solution if corrosion present.
- Measure open-circuit voltage of each cell/unit.
- Measure specific gravity of electrolyte (flooded types only) - cells should be within 0.020 of each other.
- Inspect cables and connections for wear, overheating, or damage.
- Verify battery monitoring system readings match measured values.
- Check for abnormal heat during or after charge/discharge cycle.
- Inspect vent caps for proper function (flooded types only).

5. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

PROBLEM: Low voltage reading
- Cause: Battery discharged - recharge fully and re-test.
- Cause: Poor terminal connection - clean and tighten terminals.
- Cause: Cell failure - individual cell voltage lower than others.
- Cause: Battery beyond service life - replace battery.
- Cause: Parasitic load drawing power - identify and disconnect.

PROBLEM: Will not hold charge
- Cause: Battery sulfation - attempt equalization charge (flooded types only).
- Cause: Internal short cell - replace battery.
- Cause: Charger not functioning - verify charger output, replace if needed.
- Cause: Continuous parasitic load - identify and disconnect.

PROBLEM: Overheating during charge
- Cause: Charger voltage too high - adjust charger settings.
- Cause: Battery cell short - replace battery.
- Cause: Poor ventilation - improve airflow around battery.
- Cause: High ambient temperature - reduce charge current, improve cooling.

PROBLEM: High self-discharge
- Cause: Battery self-discharge beyond specification - may need replacement.
- Cause: Parasitic load from connected system - identify and disconnect.
- Cause: Internal cell degradation - replace battery.

PROBLEM: Monitoring system shows incorrect readings
- Cause: Sensor calibration drift - recalibrate monitoring system.
- Cause: Wiring fault - inspect connections, repair or replace wires.
- Cause: Monitoring unit firmware outdated - update firmware.

6. CHARGING PROCEDURE
-----------------------
- Connect charger to battery terminals (positive to positive, negative to negative).
- Set charger to appropriate voltage and current for battery type and size.
- Begin charging - monitor voltage and current.
- Charge until voltage reaches absorption level and current drops to trickle level.
- For flooded batteries: Equalize after full charge (controlled overcharge).
- Disconnect charger: negative first, then positive.
- Record voltage and charging time in maintenance log.

7. DISCHARGING PROCEDURE
-------------------------
- Connect load to battery terminals (respect polarity).
- Monitor voltage during discharge.
- Stop discharge when voltage reaches cutoff threshold (10.5V/21.0V).
- For deep-cycle applications: Do not discharge below 50% State of Charge for longest life.
- Disconnect load: negative first, then positive.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Check voltage readings, inspect for visible issues.
- Every 50 cycles: Equalize charge (flooded types only).
- Every 100 cycles: Clean terminals, check connection tightness.
- Every 200 cycles: Measure specific gravity (flooded types), check cell voltage balance.
- Every 500 cycles: Full capacity test, verify SOH.
- Annual: Comprehensive inspection, cleaning, testing per manufacturer spec.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Acid spill: Neutralize with baking soda solution, flush with water, dispose per hazardous waste regulations.
- Battery fire: Use Class D fire extinguisher or abundant water - do not use CO2 or dry chemical.
- Severe acid exposure: Flush with water for 15 minutes, seek medical attention.
- Battery explosion hazard: Evacuate area, ventilate, do not restart.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: BMU-100 Battery Monitoring Unit
- System voltage: 12V or 24V configurable
- Capacity range: 50-1000 Ah
- Voltage measurement accuracy: ±0.1V
- Current measurement accuracy: ±2% of reading
- Temperature measurement: ±2°C
- Sampling rate: 1 reading per second
- Communication: Modbus RTU over RS-485, optional Bluetooth
- Display: 2-line LCD with real-time voltage, current, temperature, SOH
- Operating temperature: -20°C to 50°C (derating above 30°C)
- Protection class: IP65
- Connection: M8 circular connectors, screw terminals
- Alarm thresholds: Programmable, defaults at 20% SOH, voltage limits
- Certification: UL 1998, IEC 62933-1

sources.evidence:
Pump Controller Operation Manual
================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
----------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout before servicing the pump motor.
- Verify zero electrical potential at the disconnect before removing panels.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working with pressurized systems.
- Never bypass safety interlocks or emergency stop controls.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
-------------------
- The pump motor starts when the green START button is pressed.
- Motor runs until the red STOP button is pressed or an fault is detected.
- Normal operating pressure range: 20-50 PSI.
- Flow rate: 0-100 GPM depending on impeller size.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
-------------------
a. Confirm all safety guards are in place.
b. Verify lubrication oil level is between MIN and MAX marks on sight glass.
c. Confirm discharge valve is open before motor start.
d. Press GREEN START button to begin pump operation.
e. Monitor pressure gauge to confirm pressure builds within normal range.
f. Listen for unusual noises indicating cavitation or misalignment.

4. INSPECTION PHASE
-------------------
- Check pump housing for leaks, cracks, or damage.
- Inspect mechanical seals for wear or fluid seepage.
- Verify bearing temperature is within normal range (below 80°C).
- Inspect coupling alignment between motor and pump shaft.
- Check foundation bolts for tightness.
- Verify alignment laser reading is within tolerance.

5. LUBRICATION
--------------
- Oil type: ISO VG 32 synthetic compressor oil.
- Oil level: Must be between MIN and MAX marks on sight glass.
- Lubrication interval: Every 500 operating hours.
- Oil change interval: Every 2000 operating hours or annually.
- Before adding oil, clean the fill port and surrounding area.
- After oil change, prime the lubrication system and check for leaks.

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------
PROBLEM: Pump will not start
- Cause: Power not supplied - check voltage at disconnect, verify fuses.
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop station.
- Cause: Motor protection trip - reset thermal overload relay.
- Cause: Control circuit fault - inspect wiring and control relays.

PROBLEM: Low pressure output
- Cause: Discharge valve partially closed - open valve fully.
- Cause: Worn impeller - inspect and replace if necessary.
- Cause: Air leak in suction line - tighten fittings, check seals.
- Cause: Clogged filter - clean or replace filter element.

PROBLEM: Excessive vibration
- Cause: Misalignment between motor and pump - realign using laser tool.
- Cause: Unbalanced impeller - inspect and rebalance or replace.
- Cause: Worn bearings - replace bearings.
- Cause: Loose foundation bolts - tighten and re-level unit.

PROBLEM: Oil discoloration or contamination
- Cause: Oil decomposition from overheating - replace oil.
- Cause: Water ingress - inspect seals, fix leaks, replace oil.
- Cause: Foreign particles in oil - clean sumple, replace filter, flush system.

7. SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE
---------------------
a. Gradually reduce load if pump is under load.
b. Press RED STOP button to stop motor.
c. Close discharge valve after motor stops.
d. Allow pump to cool if recently under load.
e. Lockout-tagout for any subsequent maintenance.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Visual inspection for leaks, unusual noises, vibration.
- Every 500 hours: Check oil level, inspect filters, check bearing temperature.
- Every 2000 hours: Oil change, detailed inspection of seals and bearings.
- Every 5000 hours: Comprehensive overhaul, replace wear parts as needed.
- Annual: Full safety inspection, certification of interlocks and E-stops.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Pump overpressure: Immediately press E-stop, isolate power.
- Fire near pump: Evacuate area, call fire department, do not attempt extinguishment without qualified personnel.
- Chemical spill: Contain spill, notify environmental safety, follow MSDS procedures.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: PC-350 Industrial Pump Controller
- Motor power: 15 HP, 3-phase, 230/460V
- Operating temperature: -20°C to 40°C
- Protection class: IP55
- Connection: NEMA 4X enclosure
- Flow range: 5-100 GPM
- Pressure range: 20-50 PSI
- Material: Cast iron housing, stainless steel shaft

sources.evidence:
HVAC Maintenance Controller Operation Manual
============================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
---------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout on electrical power before servicing HVAC units.
- Verify zero electrical potential at disconnect before removing panels.
- Recover refrigerant per EPA regulations before opening refrigerant circuit.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working with refrigerants, electrical components, and moving parts.
- Never bypass safety controls or temperature limiters.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
--------------------
- System provides heating when heating mode is selected and thermostat calls for heat.
- System provides cooling when cooling mode is selected and thermostat calls for cool.
- Normal supply air temperature range: 55-75°F cooling, 90-120°F heating.
- Fan operates at variable speed: 0-100% depending on demand.
- Air filter should be checked monthly and replaced when dirty.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE (HEATING)
------------------------------
a. Confirm thermostat is set to HEAT mode and temperature is above current room temperature.
b. Verify gas supply is on (for gas-fired units) or electrical connections are secure (for electric units).
c. Inspect air filter - replace if dirty or restricted.
d. Check that all access panels are secure and guards are in place.
e. Set thermostat to desired temperature.
f. System should initiate ignition sequence after 30-second pre-purge.
g. Verify flame is established and burners are operating normally.
h. Monitor supply air temperature rises to normal range within 5 minutes.
i. Fan will begin blowing heated air once heat exchanger reaches safe temperature.

4. STARTUP SEQUENCE (COOLING)
-------------------------------
a. Confirm thermostat is set to COOL mode and temperature is below current room temperature.
b. Verify electrical connections are secure and power is supplied to compressor.
c. Inspect air filter - replace if dirty or restricted.
d. Check that all access panels are secure and guards are in place.
e. Set thermostat to desired temperature.
f. Compressor should start after thermostat call for cool.
g. Verify condenser fan is operating.
h. Check that supply air temperature drops to normal range within 5 minutes.
i. System will cycle on and off to maintain setpoint.

5. INSPECTION PHASE
--------------------
- Check air filter condition and airflow - replace if dirty.
- Inspect supply and return registers for obstructions.
- Check thermostat calibration and operation.
- Inspect evaporator coil for frost or ice formation (cooling mode).
- Inspect heat exchanger for cracks or damage (heating mode).
- Verify refrigerant lines for leaks (trace with detector solution).
- Check blower motor and fan for unusual noise or vibration.
- Inspect ductwork for leaks, loose connections, or damage.
- Verify safety controls are functional (limit switches, pressure controls).

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

PROBLEM: System will not start (heating)
- Cause: Thermostat not calling for heat - check settings.
- Cause: No gas supply (gas units) - verify gas valve is open.
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage at disconnect, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: Flame failure - reset after safety lockout, inspect burner.
- Cause: Limit switch tripped - reset after addressing root cause.

PROBLEM: System will not start (cooling)
- Cause: Thermostat not calling for cool - check settings.
- Cause: Compressor protection trip - reset thermal overload.
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: Refrigerant low - system may have leak, require recharge.
- Cause: High-pressure switch tripped - reset after addressing cause.

PROBLEM: Insufficient heating
- Cause: Dirty air filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Thermostat not calibrated - recalibrate or replace.
- Cause: Gas pressure too low - adjust gas valve, check supply.
- Cause: Heat exchanger restricted - clean or replace.
- Cause: Duct leaks - seal ductwork, insulate as needed.

PROBLEM: Insufficient cooling
- Cause: Dirty air filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Dirty evaporator coil - clean coil.
- Cause: Dirty condenser coil - clean outdoor unit coil.
- Cause: Refrigerant low - system has leak, locate and repair, recharge.
- Cause: High outdoor temperature - system may not meet load demand.
- Cause: Thermostat not calibrated - recalibrate or replace.

PROBLEM: Short cycling (frequent on/off)
- Cause: Oversized system for space - may require load calculation.
- Cause: Dirty filter - restrict airflow, replace filter.
- Cause: Thermostat located near heat source - relocate thermostat.
- Cause: Low refrigerant - system has leak, locate and repair, recharge.
- Cause: High static pressure in ductwork - redesign duct system.

PROBLEM: compressor will not start
- Cause: Electrical fault - check voltage, fuses, circuit breaker.
- Cause: compressor protection trip - reset thermal overload after cooling.
- Cause: capacitor failure - replace capacitor.
- Cause: contactor failure - replace contactor.
- Cause: thermostat not calling - check settings and wiring.

7. REFRIGERANT SERVICE
------------------------
- Recover refrigerant: Use certified recovery machine per EPA Section 608.
- Leak detection: Electronic leak detector or trace with Nitrogen soap solution.
- Recharge: Add only specified refrigerant type and amount per nameplate.
- Never mix refrigerant types.
- Document all refrigerant additions and removals per regulatory requirements.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Check thermostat operation, listen for unusual noises, verify airflow.
- Every 250 hours: Check air filter, inspect visual condition of unit.
- Every 500 hours: Clean or replace air filter, inspect evaporator/condenser coils.
- Every 1000 hours: Check refrigerant pressure, test safety controls, lubricate motors.
- Every 2000 hours: Clean burners (gas units), inspect heat exchanger, check belt tension.
- Annual: Full combustion analysis (gas units), refrigerant charge verification, complete safety inspection.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Refrigerant leak: Evacuate area, ventilate, call qualified HVAC technician.
- Electrical fire: Cut power at disconnect, call fire department, do not use water on electrical.
- Gas leak (gas units): Evacuate area, ventilate, do not operate electrical switches, call gas company.

10. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
----------------------------
- Model: HVAC-400 Maintenance Controller
- Capacity: 2-ton to 20-ton variable capacity
- Voltage: 208/240V single-phase or 208/3-phase
- Refrigerant: R-410A (or approved alternate)
- Airflow range: 400-2000 CFM
- Temperature range: -10°F to 120°F ambient
- Protection class: NEMA 1 (indoor), NEMA 3R (outdoor units)
- Connection: Standard HVAC plug-in connections
- Motor: ECM variable-speed blower motor
- Compressor: Scroll type, 2-20 HP

sources.evidence:
Warehouse Conveyor Controller Operation Manual
==============================================

1. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
---------------------
- Always perform lockout-tagout before servicing conveyor drive system.
- Verify zero mechanical energy stored in springs or counterweights before removing guards.
- Wear appropriate PPE when working around moving conveyors.
- Never bypass safety interlocks or emergency stop controls.
- Ensure no personnel are on or near the conveyor before startup.

2. NORMAL OPERATION
--------------------
- Conveyor starts when the green START button is pressed.
- Stops when the red STOP button is pressed or an fault is detected.
- Normal operating speed: 0-150 FPM (feet per minute).
- Load capacity: 0-5000 lbs depending on belt type.
- Belt tracking should be checked at startup and weekly.

3. STARTUP SEQUENCE
-------------------
a. Confirm all safety guards are in place and secured.
b. Verify no personnel are on the conveyor belt.
c. Confirm drive is not in manual emergency stop mode.
d. Press GREEN START button to begin conveyor operation.
e. Monitor belt tracking - adjust tracking rollers if belt centers.
f. Listen for unusual noises indicating bearing or drive issues.
g. Verify belt moves smoothly without slippage.

4. INSPECTION PHASE
-------------------
- Check belt surface for cuts, tears, or excessive wear.
- Inspect belt tracking and centering - adjust idler rollers as needed.
- Check drive belt tension - should have 1/2" deflection under firm push.
- Inspect rollers and idlers for smooth rotation and no visible damage.
- Verify safety edge sensors are functional (press to test).
- Check motor housing for overheating signs.
- Inspect chain drives for proper tension and lubrication.
- Verify emergency stop buttons are functional at all control stations.

5. LUBRICATION
--------------
- bearing lubrication: Every 250 operating hours.
- Use: Lithium-based grease, NLGI Grade 2.
- Apply to roller bearings at each bearing location.
- Grease quantity: Until slightly excess appears at seal.
- Conveyor chain: Apply chain lubricant every 500 operating hours.
- Do not over-lubricate - excess attracts dust and debris.

6. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

PROBLEM: Conveyor will not start
- Cause: Power not supplied - check voltage at disconnect, verify fuses.
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop at nearest station.
- Cause: Motor protection trip - reset thermal overload relay.
- Cause: Control circuit fault - inspect wiring and control relays.
- Cause: Belt jam preventing motor start - clear obstruction.

PROBLEM: Belt slippage
- Cause: Drive belt too loose - tighten to 1/2" deflection.
- Cause: Worn drive belt - replace with new belt.
- Cause: Contaminated belt surface - clean with appropriate solvent.
- Cause: Overloaded system - reduce load, verify capacity limits.

PROBLEM: Belt tracking issues
- Cause: Misaligned tracking rollers - adjust left/right rollers.
- Cause: Uneven belt wear - rotate or replace belt.
- Cause: Material build-up on rollers - clean roller surfaces.
- Cause: Belt damaged or stretched - replace belt.

PROBLEM: Unexpected stoppage
- Cause: Emergency stop activated - reset E-stop.
- Cause: Thermal overload trip - reset after cooling.
- Cause: Power fluctuation - check supply voltage.
- Cause: Sensor fault - inspect safety edges and limit switches.

PROBLEM: Unusual noise
- Cause: Bearing failure - replace bearings.
- Cause: Loose chain or belt tension - adjust tension.
- Cause: Foreign object in conveyor path - remove obstruction.
- Cause: Motor mounting loose - tighten mounting bolts.

7. SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE
---------------------
a. Gradually reduce load if conveyor is under load.
b. Press RED STOP button to stop motor.
c. Allow belt to come to complete stop.
d. Lockout-tagout for any subsequent maintenance.
e. Remove any remaining material from belt.

8. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
------------------------
- Daily: Visual inspection for wear, tracking, unusual noises.
- Every 250 hours: Lubricate bearings, check belt tension.
- Every 500 hours: Inspect belt surface, clean rollers, test E-stops.
- Every 1000 hours: Replace drive belt, lubricate chain.
- Every 2000 hours: Comprehensive inspection of all rollers and idlers.
- Annual: Full safety certification of interlocks and E-stops.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
------------------------
- Person on conveyor: Immediately press E-stop, do not attempt rescue until motion stops.
- Fire near conveyor: Evacuate area, call fire department.
- Material spill: Stop conveyor, contain spill, clean per warehouse protocols.
